title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
slides: Microsoft built its own AI chip. Will Nvidia lose its grip?
Maia 100 powers Azure AI workloads, not rivals
Yet it still rents Nvidia GPUs for top models
Your cloud bill may drop where Maia fits
Ask your vendor which chips run your AI today
thread_text:
1. Microsoft's silicon gamble

Microsoft just built its own AI chip, Maia 100, to power Azure workloads instead of buying every GPU from Nvidia. The cloud giant is quietly hedging its bets.

2. Maia stays in-house

Maia 100 runs Microsoft's own AI services, not sold to rivals. It's a vertical play: optimize cost and supply for Azure, not compete in the merchant chip market.

3. Nvidia still on speed dial

For cutting-edge models, Microsoft still rents Nvidia GPUs. Maia handles scale, but top-tier training and inference remain Nvidia's turf for now.

4. Your bill could shrink

Where Maia fits, Azure can pass savings on compute. If your AI workloads match its sweet spot, expect lower cloud costs without switching providers.

5. Ask your vendor

Which chips run your AI today? Ask your cloud provider or AI vendor. If they can't name the silicon, you don't know your cost or supply risk.
